module: Module that populates a spline with decal instances (DecalData + engine instances) along its length, for the Decal Spline tool. It samples the spline by arc length with a step of (4.0 m decal length + spline.spacing), distributes the components (materials) alternately or randomly according to their probability, orients each decal with the Frenet frame, Z jitter and pre-rotation, and places it in the middle of its cell. It maintains the shared DecalData templates in a "DecalSpline - Templates ..." SimGroup under MissionGroup, with instance counters to delete a template that has become unused.
notes: Assumed length of a decal: 4.0 m (decalLength constant). Decals are centered quads.
The templates are registered with scenetree.decalPersistMan (file editor.getDecalDataFilePath()) to be saved.
Instances are created with editor.addDecalInstanceWithTan(position, up, tangent, template, scale, frame, 3, 1).
If the templates folder no longer exists, populateDecalSpline recreates it and first clears the decals of all splines passed in splines, then resets the internal tables.
A spline with fewer than 2 divPoints is not populated.

populateDecalSpline.desc: Creates the decal instances along the spline, creating the DecalData templates as needed (texRows, texCols, material).

spline.desc: decal spline (divPoints, tangents, normals, spacing, jitter, components 1 to 4...)

splines.desc: all splines, cleaned if the templates folder must be recreated

tryRemove.desc: Removes the spline's decal instances from the scene (editor.deleteDecalInstance), decrements the counters then deletes the templates whose counter drops below 1.

removeFolder.desc: Deletes the folder (SimGroup) of the shared templates, unless decals kept by a locked spline during a Lua reload still use it.

hasAny.desc: Indicates whether the tool holds decals for this spline.

returns.desc: true if at least one instance exists

release.desc: For a Lua reload: lets go of the decals of a locked spline without deleting them and returns their uids by material, with the templates used and the folder id, so that adopt() can take them back. Their templates stay counted.

adopt.desc: Takes back the decals released by release() that are still present in the scene (found by uid via Engine.Render.DecalMgr), with their templates and their folder, and restores the counters.

propagateRowsCols.desc: When rows/columns (numRows/numCols) change for a component, copies these values to the other components that use the same material and clamps their frame to numRows*numCols-1.

componentIdx.desc: number of the modified component, from 1 to 4
